errors.quote: stop when donor-level precision reaches a prespecified range
errors.issue: Repeated outcome-dependent precision stopping can change interval coverage. Specify a validated blinded variance re-estimation or sequential procedure and include the actual stopping rule in calibration; a fixed range alone is insufficient.

errors.quote: the p-value distribution should be approximately uniform under permutation
errors.issue: At very small donor n valid exact p-values can be discrete/conservative. Assess attained size and coverage using the actual randomization space rather than requiring approximate uniformity.

errors.quote: A treatment effect claim should be accepted only if:
errors.issue: The seven listed conditions describe design/reporting validity but omit a criterion based on estimated effect magnitude and uncertainty. A well-reported precisely null result could satisfy every listed condition; distinguish valid analysis from support for an effect.
Preserve treatment-arm sampling and complete matched structures, not just donor labels and strata. Unrestricted small-n bootstraps can have no observations in an arm.

errors.quote: held-out validation cannot be performed or fails
errors.issue: Lack of a feasible holdout limits generalization but does not itself downgrade every prespecified calibrated confirmatory treatment test to exploratory. The answer acknowledges small-n validity elsewhere but this acceptance rule conflicts.

rationale: Useful donor-level design, restricted permutations, hierarchical simulation, held-out preprocessing and honest confounding limits. Precision stopping is not error-controlled and the acceptance gate does not establish an effect, requiring substantive decision-rule repairs.

Independent treatment replication is at the assignment level; subsamples can improve donor measurement without creating assignments. Between-donor treatment regression is identifiable; saturated donor fixed indicators would instead absorb donor-constant treatment.
High ICC or loss of significance is not proof of a false effect. Small independent n limits precision and approximation robustness, not automatic invalidation of every prespecified model.
Equal-donor, observed-cell-weighted and nonlinear conditional coefficients can have different estimands. State normalization, link and standardization before comparing methods.

Ordinary bootstrap is not a null sample. Null simulations need explicit no-effect generation, parameter uncertainty and repeated datasets to assess false-positive frequency; a single permuted dataset is not an empirical FPR estimate.

Respect actual randomization restrictions and joint pair/block sampling. Sharp-null randomization exactness does not automatically transfer to all average-effect nulls. Report coarse attainable p resolution with few assignments.

Held-out prediction and confirmatory effect inference differ. A lack of external holdout limits validation but does not invalidate a prespecified calibrated treatment test. All data-dependent preprocessing must remain inside development folds.
